Misanthrope

MIS-an-throhp · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Misanthrope is a person who dislikes or distrusts humankind in general.

Everyone in the apartment building agreed that the man in 4B was a misanthrope -- he'd lived there for a decade and never once said hello.

Worked Example

The critic's memoir revealed him to be a genuine misanthrope, someone who found nearly every human interaction exhausting and preferred the company of his houseplants.

A misanthrope is a person who dislikes or distrusts people generally -- not just one annoying neighbor, but humanity as a whole.

Antonyms

philanthropist

philanthropist: someone devoted to promoting others' welfare

socialite

socialite: a person very active in fashionable society

How Strong Is It? — loner → curmudgeon → misanthrope

loner vs. misanthrope

loner vs. misanthrope: A loner simply prefers solitude, without necessarily disliking people.

curmudgeon vs. misanthrope

curmudgeon vs. misanthrope: A curmudgeon is a habitually grumpy, easily annoyed person -- similar in spirit, but focused on temperament rather than a settled dislike of humanity.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — mis-

root — mis-: hatred, dislike (Greek misos)

root — anthrope

root — anthrope: human being (Greek anthropos)

Put it together

Put it together: Misanthrope comes from Greek misos ('hatred') + anthropos ('human being') -- literally 'a hater of humankind.'

Use the root in a new word: anthropology

Use the root in a new word: anthropology: She's fascinated by anthropology, the study of human societies and cultures throughout history.

Root Check

Word Choice

Misanthrope describes a person's general attitude toward humanity as a whole -- different from being irascible (quick-tempered with individuals) or holding rancor (a bitter feeling toward someone specific); a misanthrope's dislike is broad and impersonal, aimed at people in general.
